answer: Each epoch the network draws a public beacon and keeps a genealogy tree, scoring each head at the vertex where its own birth chain was signed. A head forked after that beacon is a hollow shell and scores nothing; only heads already born before it, each with its own keypair and its own prior-epoch signatures, count. That signed history is scarce per head and cannot be cloned, lent, or minted in bulk when a flood arrives, so a farm's extra head must be a separate coral on the reef, rooted in its own tide of past epochs, not one more core running one more copy.
